ORAL JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.6218/2016 dated 16.12.2017 by the XXII Addl. Small Causes Judge and XX ACMM and Member, MACT, Bengaluru, the Insurance Company as well as the claimant are before this Court.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has filed MFA.No.1428/2018 and the claimant has filed MFA.No.1171/2020.
The claim petition is filed by the son of the deceased seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.25,00,000/- for the death of the deceased.

2. It is the case of the claimant that on 25.07.2016 at about 3.30 pm., the deceased was waiting to cross the road near Magadi-Bangalore Main road, Chikkagollarahatti bus stand, DasanapuraHobli,
Bangalore North Taluk, at that time the tempo was coming from Bangalore towards Magadi being driven by its driver rashly and negligently with high speed, endangering to human life and property and dashed against the NC: 2025:KHC:35411 HC-KAR deceased.
Due to impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately she was shifted to Sree Ram Hospital, Sunkadakatte, in the said hospital doctors made best efforts, but the injured succumbed to death on the same day.
The Tribunal had taken the income at Rs.2,000/- and awarded the compensation as per the table given below.

Sl. Heads Rs. Compensation  No. amount  awarded  1. Loss of dependency Rs. 1,68,000/-
 2. Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
 3. Transportation of body, Rs. 15,000/-
 funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses Manjunatha vs Harish on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103493392/
3
Total Rs

3 . When it comes to the liability, it is the case of Insurance Company that the driver is having a license to drive a LMV non-transport vehicle, but the vehicle that he was driving is a transport vehicle as such the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
That contention is negatived by the Tribunal.
Aggrieved thereby the Insurance Company is before this Court and the claimant is seeking enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC:35411 HC-KAR 4.

Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that as there is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and as he is not having a valid driving licence, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal had rightly considered and granted the compensation and no interference is called for.
5.
Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that as this accident had taken place in the year 2016, the Tribunal ought to have taken the income at Rs.9,500/- per month.
It is submitted that as the son is the dependent and the Tribunal ought to have taken the income as per the table and ought to have granted the compensation.
6. In response to that, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the claimant is the son of the deceased, who is 37 years old and he cannot be termed as a dependent.

He relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Vinish Jain and others1.

Vs. Birender3 and had considered the claimant as the dependent.

sentences.text: 8. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.
First coming to the contention of the Insurance Company with regard to the LMV transport and non transport, this issue is no more res-integra.
In the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan V/s Oriental Insurance company Ltd.4, still the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: Then coming to the compensation, the deceased is 61 years and the claimant is her son.
This Court, considering the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Seema Rani's case referred supra is inclined to consider the son as a dependent.

As this accident was occurred in the year 2016, as per the table for the year 2016, this Court is taking the income at Rs.9,500/- per month, 50% of it comes Manjunatha vs Harish on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103493392/

10.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.Mekala vs. M.
